title: 再審見直しの法務省案「検察の、検察による…」　稲田氏が批判
extracted_text: 確定した刑事裁判をやり直す再審制度の見直しを巡り、自民党の稲田朋美元政調会長が毎日新聞のインタビューに応じた。法務省が自民に示した案のままでは「検察の、検察による、検察のための法律」だと批判。法務省・検察庁に厳しい姿勢を続けていては「いつか検察に刺されるぞ」と心配する声が党内にあることについては「だからと言って、社会正義に反することは許せない」と語り、冤罪（えんざい）被害者の早期救済に向け「検察対自民党」の戦いを続けるとした。 再審見直しの法務省案を協議する4月6日の自民会合冒頭で「マスコミが出た（退出した）後では1ミリも私たちの言うことを聞かないじゃないですか！」と声を張り上げ、再審論議の世論の関心を高めるきっかけとなった稲田氏。「私以外にも、みんなが毎回毎回激しい訴えを続けている。でも、法務省はかたくな。だから不規則発言を試みた」と振り返った。 法務省案の最大の問題点は、裁判所による再審開始（裁判やり直し）の決定に対して検察官が不服を申し立てる制度（検察官抗告）を存続させる内容であることだと指摘。再審制度は裁判のやり直しを認めるか否かを審議する再審請求審と、実際に裁判をやり直す再審公判の2階建てだとし、「非公開で行われる1階部分の再審請求審で、検察が機械的に抗告を繰り返すから時間がかかる」と訴えた。そして「検察は不服があるなら公開の再審公判で有罪を主張すべきだ」とした。 法務省が後に示した修正案を巡っては「話にならない。十分な理由がなければ抗告しないなんて当たり前だ」と一蹴。参院では少数与党であることも踏まえ、野党も理解を示すような実効性ある見直しを進めることこそ「高市政権の助けになる」と訴えた。【宮島寛、安部志帆子】
translated_text: LDP former Policy Research Council Chairman Inada Tomomo responded to an interview with the Mainichi Shimbun regarding the review of the retrial system for finalized criminal cases. She criticized the Ministry of Justice's proposal presented to the LDP, saying it would result in "a law by prosecutors, for prosecutors." Regarding voices within the party expressing concern that maintaining a tough stance toward the Ministry of Justice and the Prosecutors' Office would eventually "backfire on us," she stated, "That said, we cannot allow anything that goes against social justice." She declared her intention to continue the fight against the Ministry and the LDP to secure early relief for victims of wrongful convictions. At the outset of the April 6 LDP meeting to discuss the Ministry's retrial reform proposal, Inada raised her voice, saying, "After the media walks out, they don't listen to a single word we say!" Her outspoken criticism helped bring public attention to the retrial debate. She reflected that she wasn't the only one making forceful arguments at every meeting, but the Ministry remained stubbornly resistant, prompting her to make provocative statements. The core problem with the Ministry's proposal is that it preserves the system allowing prosecutors to file objections to court decisions granting retrials. She emphasized the two-tier structure of the retrial system—initial closed hearings on retrial requests and subsequent open retrial proceedings—and argued that prosecutors should present their case in the public proceedings rather than filing mechanical objections during closed hearings. She rejected the subsequent revised proposal as insufficient, asserting that not objecting without sufficient grounds should be self-evident. She called for effective reform that gains understanding from opposition parties, noting the administration's narrow majority in the Upper House, saying this would "strengthen the Abe administration."
title_en: Inada Criticizes Ministry of Justice Retrial Reform Plan as "By Prosecutors, For Prosecutors"
